answer: Entry by bonded vouching turns identity into a liability: a new agent may enter the harbor only when an established agent vouches for it and locks collateral in escrow, mapped in a public atlas of who vouched for whom. A genuine identity is a pearl, rare and costly to fake, because each voucher risks its own stake if its protege cheats, so honest agents vouch sparingly. A sybil farmer must either buy many expensive vouches or burn its own collateral on every fake, and the cost of one fake identity stays equal to the cost of one real one.
